correctness.rationale: Every restricted character inner product is explicitly evaluated as a finite sum on the exponent hyperplane \(\sum u_i=b\pmod{q-1}\); it is zero across diagonal-shift orbits and unit-modulus within them. Therefore every occupied orbit is a rank-one all-ones Gram block. The occupancy formula divides the \(d!/(\prod n_c!)\) ordered words by the free \(q-1\)-element diagonal action. Covering and pigeonhole arguments separately prove exact injectivity, surjectivity, and all positive eigenlevels, including \(k=0,d\). Independent orbit/occupancy enumeration passes 124 cases and direct complex Gram diagonalization passes 56 cases, maximum error \(6.67\times10^{-15}\). The proof, not experiments, covers all prime powers and dimensions.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge claim-to-claim comparison: the 2019 Hamming-variety extension theorem calculates large-scale \(L^2\)-to-\(L^r\) extension bounds and additive Fourier decay, not the exact all-degree multiplicative-character band Gram spectrum or its sharp orthogonality and interpolation cutoffs. A publicly readable all-degree Fourier sampling theorem for q-ary Hamming **weight shells** concerns a different constraint, and its Krawtchouk eigenvalues do not directly imply the diagonal-shift occupancy law for a fixed nonzero coordinate product. The standard subgroup-character orthogonality principle explains why some columns coincide, but leaves the exact spectral occupancy multiplicities and simultaneous sharp transitions to be determined. Multiple semantically focused searches detected no matching theorem. Priority beyond the inspected material remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The whole family of interaction-order sampling operators on the Hamming multiplicative hypersurface is a natural Fourier-restriction hierarchy motivated by finite-field extension theory. The theorem settles its entire eigenvalue census at every degree, determines the first unavoidable column dependence and the precise interpolation cutoff, and exhibits an exact orthonormal half-degree interpolation basis for every odd-dimensional ternary case. The integer-level emergence thresholds give direct quantitative bounds on normalized coefficient-frame stability and distinguish a complete band from an overcomplete one. These are complete structural classifications and sharp natural invariants, not an arbitrary single dimension or a numerical table; no claim is made that they solve general \(L^p\) extension or noisy inversion.
